The Johnson harmonic dimensions binom(n,j)-binom(n,j-1) sum to binom(n,k). Explicit coefficient extraction gives zero exactly for odd m when a=0, hence rank binom(2k,k)/2; all coefficients at a=1,2 are nonzero. Elementary monotonicity yields the two exact sharp condition numbers and the Stirling asymptotics. Independently rebuilt binary-intersection matrices and diagonalized each n=2k+a for k=1,2,3 and a=0,1,2; multiplicities, nullities and condition numbers match. These finite checks do not prove the universal theorem; the harmonic argument does.
